response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT f.orderslink AS orderslink, o.dealedge AS side, AVG(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS avg_net_fee_rate, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009 GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.dealedge), s AS (SELECT g.*, AVG(avg_net_fee_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY side) AS side_avg FROM g) SELECT orderslink, side, avg_net_fee_rate, record_count, avg_net_fee_rate - side_avg AS diff_from_side_avg FROM s WHERE avg_net_fee_rate > side_avg ORDER BY diff_from_side_avg DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: 'High-rate' with 0.0009 as the cutoff means feerate >= 0.0009 (the cutoff itself is included).
Record count is the number of fee rows in the group (COUNT(*)), including rows where rebrate is null. The average net fee rate skips those rows because feerate - rebrate is null.
The side average is the unweighted mean of the group averages. Groups whose average is null are ignored.
orders.recordvault is unique, so the join does not duplicate fee rows.

alternatives.interpretation: High-rate means strictly above the cutoff (feerate > 0.0009).
